minutes.headline: Conservation Commission continued most hearings to Jan 8, approved a septic repair and a lake wall amendment, and added $5,500 to an RTP grant.
minutes.summary: The commission met by Zoom and worked through continuations, new and continued hearings, a violations update and a grant update. A septic upgrade at 48 Arbor Street and a retaining wall amendment at 12 Horizon Island Road were approved with conditions, and several other matters were continued to January 8. Members also discussed paint stewardship, a farmland-of-local-importance program, Chapter 61 notification and the permit extension act.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; none was seen.

votes.outcome: passed 4-0 by roll call (Jenny, Mike, Chris, chair all aye)

votes.motion: Approve the notice of intent for 48 Arbor Street septic upgrade with special conditions: silt fence added to straw wattle, and buffer placards along the 30-foot line
Continue 50 Pine Grove Road hearing to January 8
Have Sophia send the original March 2023 determination to DEP and clarify the September copy was a misunderstanding
Continue 400 Leominster-Shirley Road matter to January 8
Continue the stormwater management notice of intent (Electric Ave and Pierce) to January 8
Approve amendment of order of conditions at 12 Horizon Island Road, with conditions: work during lake drawdown and sand pulled back onto shore
Reject the certificate of compliance for 57 Round Road, citing need for a change notice
Approve additional amount for wetland delineation and lot line staking under the RTP 2023 grant, from the Timber rights fund

budget_items.what_was_said: A request for additional funds to add wetland delineation and lot line staking was approved; the chair said there was room in the grant to absorb it and that it would be paid from the Timber rights fund.
Greg Roy explained the additions were not due to the project being over budget, since work had not begun.

budget_items.topic: Table Rock parking lot design and bids
budget_items.what_was_said: Greg suggested bidding more parking spaces and reducing later if bids come in too high.
The monthly budget report is to be uploaded to the share drive around the 15th of each month.
The program is funded by a small fee at the point of sale, and a member later mentioned a charge at drop-off.

transfers.description: Additional wetland delineation and lot line staking cost for the RTP grant proposed to come out of the Timber rights fund

decisions.decision: Applicant at 50 Pine Grove Road asked to consider moving the shed outside the 50 feet, show the fifth tree and any stairs, and give deck material details before the January 8 hearing.

Members verbally endorsed the chair acting as signatory for the Farmland of Local Importance program, pending no objection from the select board, open space committee and agricultural commission; a formal vote would follow.
Paint stewardship recommendation deferred to a future meeting so members can read the materials.
Sophia to arrange a call with the town contact about the 4 Fire Road 12 violation and open conditions on town land.
The 1168 Mass Ave violation was bumped to the next meeting because no owner attended.
The 950 Chase Road shed matter stays on the tracking list pending the select board.
January schedule is January 8, 22 and 29, with the lake reports on the 29th.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission approved a septic upgrade at 48 Arbor Street with special conditions, 4-0 on a roll call.
It approved an amendment to the order of conditions at 12 Horizon Island Road, requiring work during lake drawdown, 4-0.
It voted 4-0 to approve added wetland delineation and lot line staking under the RTP 2023 grant, paid from the Timber rights fund.
The commission rejected the certificate of compliance for 57 Round Road, citing the need for a change notice, 4-0.
Hearings for 390 Howard Street, 50 Pine Grove Road, 400 Leominster-Shirley Road and the Electric Ave stormwater filing were each continued to January 8.

why_it_matters: Wetland and shoreline projects near homes, such as septic repairs and lake walls, move through this commission, and most of the open ones now wait until January 8.
The extra grant work was paid from the Timber rights fund, not the general budget, so it does not touch the tax bill directly as heard in the minutes.
watch_next: January 8 hearings on the continued matters, including 50 Pine Grove Road, where the applicant was asked to revise plans.
A formal vote on the chair signing for the Farmland of Local Importance program, and a later decision on the paint stewardship recommendation.
